title: Implicit elimination of unit-twisted formal monoid variables
statement:
Let $(D,\mathfrak n)$ be a nonzero complete Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and let $S,T$ be fine saturated monoids [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] which are sharp, meaning that $0$ is the only invertible element of each. Let $ eta:S	o T$ be a homomorphism with $ eta^{-1}(0)=\{0\}$. For such a sharp monoid $P$, write $D[[P]]$ for the completion of the monoid ring $D[P]$, with basis $[p]$ and multiplication $[p][p']=[p+p']$, at $(\mathfrak n,[p]:p
e0)$. Put $H=D[[S\oplus T]]$, and denote its $S$- and $T$-monomials by $X^s$ and $Y^t$. Let $u:S	o D[[S]]^	imes$ be a homomorphism to the multiplicative group of units. Let $I$ be the ideal of $H$ generated by $X^s-u(s)Y^{ eta(s)}$ for $s\in S$. The map $D[[T]]	o H/I$ induced by coefficients and $Y$-monomials is a continuous isomorphism. Its inverse sends every $X^s$ with $s
e0$ into the ideal $(Y^t:t
e0)$, and induces the identity on $D$ after killing all nonzero $T$-monomials. A local ring has a unique maximal ideal; complete means that its canonical map to its maximal-ideal completion is an isomorphism. Here $S\oplus T=S	imes T$ with componentwise addition.

source.place: ILO VI 2.3, printed pp.72--73, the character action and formal monoid chart formula. The implicit substitution with arbitrary chart unit twists is an agent-formulated algebraic refinement, not asserted verbatim in ILO.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-formal-monoid-implicit-elimination] to the same $(D,\mathfrak n)$, $S$, $T$, $\beta$ and $u$. Its hypotheses are identical: $D$ is nonzero complete Noetherian local; $S,T$ are sharp fine saturated; $\beta^{-1}(0)=\{0\}$; and $u$ is a homomorphism to $D[[S]]^\times$. Its notation $D[[P]]$ uses exactly the same monoid-ring completion ideal, so its $H$ and $I$ are the $H$ and $I$ here. Its conclusion gives precisely the continuous coefficient-and-$Y$-monomial isomorphism $D[[T]]\to H/I$, the inverse image of each $X^s$ for $s\ne0$ in $(Y^t:t\ne0)$, and the identity on $D$ after killing the nonzero $T$-monomials. The final sentences of this item only explain local completeness and the direct-sum notation; they add no assertion beyond these definitions.
